sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ever wished you could add or subtract 1 from a variable with just one character? That’s exactly what increment and decrement operators do!

• How `++` and `--` make your code shorter and cleaner
• The difference between `i++` and `++i` (it’s sneaky!)
• Where these operators shine in real programs

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine you’re counting apples in a basket. Every time you add one apple, you could say `apples = apples + 1`. But what if you could just say `apples++`? That’s the magic of these operators!

These operators come in two flavors:
• **Postfix** (`i++`, `i--`): Use the value first, then change it
• **Prefix** (`++i`, `--i`): Change the value first, then use it

They might look similar, but they behave differently when used in expressions. Let’s break it down:

sections.title: 📊 Visual Simulation
sections.content: Step-by-step visualization of how Increment and Decrement Operators works:

steps.title: Postfix Increment (i++)
steps.description: The original value is used first, then incremented. Like taking a photo before adding an apple to the basket.
steps.code:
int i = 3;
int j = i++; // j gets 3, then i becomes 4

steps.title: Prefix Increment (++i)
steps.description: The value is incremented first, then used. Like adding an apple before taking the photo.
steps.code:
int i = 3;
int j = ++i; // i becomes 4, then j gets 4

steps.title: Standalone Use
steps.description: When used alone, both forms do the same thing. It’s only in expressions where the difference matters!
steps.code:
i++; // i becomes 4
++i; // i becomes 5 (same effect)

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ `--i` and `i--` work the same way but subtract 1
✓ Standalone use? Both forms are identical!
✓ Avoid using them in complex expressions - it gets messy fast!

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Use `i++` when you need the original value first
Use `++i` when you want the new value immediately
Keep it simple - one operator per line is clearer
donts: Don’t use `i++ + ++i` - it’s confusing and error-prone
Don’t mix them in long expressions
Don’t forget they modify the variable permanently!
sections.protip: When in doubt, split it into two lines: `int j = i; i++;` is clearer than `int j = i++;`

problem.description:
What will this code print? Try to guess before running it!

Then, modify the code to use prefix operators instead of postfix and see how the output changes.
hints: Remember: postfix uses the value first, then increments
Prefix increments first, then uses the value
The value of `a` changes in both cases!
problem.explanation: The first case uses postfix, so `b` gets the original value of `a` (5) before `a` increments to 6. The second case uses prefix, so `a` increments to 6 first, then `b` gets that new value.

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 `i++` and `++i` both add 1, but behave differently in expressions
📌 Postfix (`i++`): use first, then change. Prefix (`++i`): change first, then use
📌 Practice with simple examples to master the difference
📌 Ready to use these in loops and counters next!
